name: HASTIE, the Hon. Andrew William

headline.note: Contemporaneous reporting dates SAS resignation to 21 August 2015. Defence-hosted first-person evidence now fixes three years at ADFA and one at Duntroon; institutional evidence establishes salaried ADFA cadet service and a public professional profile dates Duntroon to January-December 2006. Exact 2003 entry, leave and payroll-transition dates still prevent headline calculation.

career_spells.employer: Australian Defence Force, ADFA and Royal Military College Duntroon
career_spells.evidence_note: Hastie's Defence-hosted 2022 speeches expressly date his Army career to 2003–2015 and describe three years at ADFA followed by one year at Duntroon. A statutory ADFA review describes cadets as salaried ADF members in a residential military-training and university program, while his public professional profile dates Duntroon January–December 2006. Together these support substantive full-time paid military training, not a separate university job. The exact 2003 entry date, leave and ADFA-to-Duntroon payroll boundary remain unverified; five earlier years of youth cadets are separate unpaid participation.
career_spells.counting_note: Substantive full-time paid training is supported, but start-day precision, leave and the internal transition boundary remain insufficient for a certified headline total. Study and military service are not duplicated.

career_spells.employer: Australian Army, 2nd Cavalry Regiment and Special Air Service Regiment
career_spells.evidence_note: Official officer range starts 2007; own interview explicitly describes resignation from full-time Army in August 2015. Deployments and SAS transfer are roles within the same employer, not additional overlapping jobs. ABC 21 August 2015 reports resignation that day, corroborated by Friday wording in The West. Boundary records resignation event; final paid day/terminal leave unverified. ABC identifies Operation Sovereign Borders advisory duties, treated within Army service rather than a separate civilian job. Personal November 2020 article dates posting to SASR as a non-qualified captain to January 2010. This narrows internal unit chronology, rather than Army entry or paid cessation; subsequent qualification date is not supplied.
career_spells.counting_note: Full-time status supported by first-person statement. Resignation day now documented, but start-day precision, final payroll/leave and continuity are unresolved. No assumed 1 January start or duplicate deployment/advisory years.

research_notes: 2026-10-01 avenues: official frozen range, Defence employer biography, own formal biography, direct reported 2016 interview, ABC transition report, secondary reserve chronology and targeted full-time searches. Army Research Centre contributor page supplies no substantive biography.

Obtain precise reserve-to-regular transfer, ADFA and Duntroon salaried-service periods, commissioning date, actual separation date and non-service breaks. Determine whether earlier paid civilian work exists.

Calculation note: the 2007 to August 2015 officer labels imply an elapsed boundary envelope of approximately 7.58–8.67 years (earliest/latest calendar boundaries, days divided by 365.2425); this is not a certified continuous full-time-years total, does not include pre-2007 training and is not written into the headline. No new aggregation convention is introduced.
Do not count inactive standby membership after August 2015 as full-time service. Part-time UNSW Regiment service is separate; do not sum deployment durations on top of Army tenure.

Follow-up 2026-10-02: ABC contemporaneous today resignation statement and The West Friday corroboration resolve August resignation event to 21 August 2015. This is not proof of final paid day. Own cadet speech supplies primary 2003 Army start context and separates five earlier years of youth cadets.

Secondary December 2006 commissioning claim remains in tension with frozen officer range from 2007; searches for individual Duntroon graduation/personnel evidence did not resolve it. A general December graduation ceremony cannot establish personal commissioning. Existing conditional August boundary envelope remains a broad earlier envelope, not certified total.

Targeted first-job/full-time/personnel and court-domain searches did not establish civilian employment or an individual training contract. ABC local-law-firm first-job quotation belongs to Matt Keogh, not Hastie.

Follow-up 2026-10-03: Defence-hosted first-person evidence establishes a three-year ADFA plus one-year Duntroon sequence; statutory review evidence establishes that ADFA cadets were salaried ADF members undertaking residential military and academic training. A publicly indexed professional profile supplies January-December 2006 for Duntroon. These support full-time paid training status but not a certified 2003 start day, leave record or internal payroll transition. Next: individual appointment/commissioning record, final payroll and non-service breaks.

Follow-up2026-10-04: Personal article supplies month-level January 2010 SASR posting within existing Army service. Commissioning/ADFA-entry/payroll and early civilian-work searches did not find an individual service document. LinkedIn indexed January 2003 YOFT quotation is a displayed comment without demonstrated subject attribution and is not adopted as Hastie entry date. Reserve-to-regular transfer, precise 2003 start, December 2006 commissioning claim, non-service breaks and final payroll remain gaps; retain unknown totals.

Follow-up2026-10-05: ANU-hosted first-person podcast transcript identifies previously omitted GeorgeWashingtonUniversity shortcourse in2007; added excludedstudy separate from Army payroll. Secondaryprogramme title not attributed to primarysource. Exactname/commissioning searches still no individual2006commission order; do not adopt general12Decemberceremony as personalappointment. Study overlaps existingArmyyear; no unpaidleave assumed. Next individual service entry/separation or commission record and course provider dates.
